title: Demo staffing: an app has no way to declare the demo accounts its seed data is dealt to — every app re-writes a local "create users, assign positions, re-evaluate sharing" script (HotCRM has one; hotclm needs the same)
body:
Filing class: ③ platform gap, filed at destination from an app ruling. Reader: `domain:server` / auth + sharing triage. Unlabelled, no assignee. Origin: objectstack-ai/hotclm#28, ruled **D** by the maintainer on 2026-10-25 (ruling comment https://github.com/objectstack-ai/hotclm/issues/28#issuecomment-6396320437): "demo accounts are the platform's to create; the app only declares them".

## Context

A metadata app's demo seed deals records to named people: hotclm's 120 contracts and 143 obligations go to `Business Requester 1/2/3`, the legal rows to `Legal Counsel 1/2`. The seed cannot create a user (by design — `sys_user` writes are refused by the ADR-0092 guard and a seeded row could not sign in anyway), so a fresh `pnpm demo` boots with exactly one account (the dev admin from `maybeSeedDevAdmin`), which holds no app permission set and sees an empty navigation. The operator must read the README, create five accounts in Setup with the names spelled exactly, then re-run the seed so the deferred `owner_id` references resolve. One mistyped character leaves the owner NULL with nothing but a deferred-reference ERROR in the boot log.

## What apps do today

HotCRM wrote `scripts/demo-staff.ts` (its #640): `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/create-user` per person, `sys_user_position` rows, **re-evaluate every active sharing rule**, then sign in as each demo user and assert the three layers connect; localhost-only, idempotent, names kept in a file the stack config never imports so they never reach a real deployment. hotclm would be the second copy, hotsrm the third. The step every copy must get right is a platform-internal fact: `plugin-sharing` materialises grants from the record write hook, which returns early for `isSystem` writes, so seeded rows carry no grants until a rule is re-evaluated — "assign the position" alone is silently not enough.

## The gap

There is no platform primitive for "the demo accounts this app's seed assumes". The platform already has the one-user version of it (`maybeSeedDevAdmin` mints a loginable admin on a dev boot) but nothing an app can declare.

## What is asked

A declarative demo-staffing primitive, shape the platform's to choose, e.g. in the stack definition:

```ts
demo: {
  staff: [
    { name: 'Business Requester 1', email: 'requester1@demo.local', position: undefined, permissionSets: ['clm_requester'] },
    { name: 'Legal Counsel 1', position: 'legal_counsel' },
    …
  ],
}
```

applied by `os dev` / `os demo` (or the dev-admin seeding step) **only on a local boot**, idempotently: create through the auth door, assign positions / permission sets, re-evaluate sharing rules, verify each account can sign in and reach its navigation, refuse to run against a non-local URL. Seed datasets then resolve `owner_id` by name on the first boot, with no second run and no README step. The list must not be part of the built artifact (same discipline as HotCRM's `demo-staffing.ts`).

Verification checklist for the implementer: HotCRM `scripts/demo-staff.ts`'s four steps, as measured there.

## Dedupe

`search_issues` on this repo for demo accounts / staffing / seeded users: #25083, #24409, #14157, #14349, #15337 — all about the dev admin, SSO setup users or lock-out on seeded people directories; **0** about an app-declared demo staff list. objectstack#16712 (positions inserted after bootstrap do not resolve permissions) is adjacent and is the reason step 3 exists.

## Not asked

- No seeding of `sys_user` through datasets (§10 of hotclm's design and the ADR-0092 guard both forbid it; this primitive goes through the auth door).
- No app-side script in hotclm while this is open (its AGENTS.md → Platform gaps); hotclm#28 is `Blocked-by` this card.
